overview: Ecolab is the global leader in water, hygiene, and infection-prevention solutions and services, providing chemistry, digital monitoring equipment, and technical expertise to customers in foodservice, food & beverage processing, hospitality, healthcare, industrial (including data centers), and life sciences markets. The company operates a razor/razor-blade model combining consumable chemicals with dispensing equipment, digital sensors, and on-site service technicians, generating highly recurring revenue across roughly 170 countries. Its March 2026 agreement to acquire CoolIT Systems (liquid cooling for AI data centers, ~$4.75B) extends the model into a new high-growth adjacency within its Global High-Tech/Global Water business.

business_model.summary: Ecolab sells an integrated bundle of specialty chemicals, dispensing/dosing equipment, digital monitoring (e.g., water and energy management sensors), and on-site service/technical expertise, priced typically as a service contract rather than a one-off product sale. Revenue is largely recurring (consumables replenished continuously, multi-year service relationships) with high customer switching costs due to embedded equipment, regulatory compliance needs, and technician relationships. Reported net sales were $16.08B in FY2025, up from $15.74B in FY2024; the trailing-twelve-month run rate through Q2 2026 is roughly $16.8B, with organic growth accelerating to ~5% in H1 2026 and second-half 2026 guidance of 6-7% organic growth.
business_model.customer_type: B2B - large enterprise, industrial, institutional and hospitality/foodservice customers; increasingly hyperscale data center operators via CoolIT
business_model.geographic_mix: North America is the largest region (roughly half of sales), with the balance spread across Europe, Latin America, Asia Pacific, and other international markets; ~170 countries served

main_competitors: Vertiv/Schneider Electric (data center cooling, via CoolIT)
competitive_position.market_position: Global #1 in water treatment/hygiene chemicals and services; long-standing category leader since the 2011 Nalco acquisition consolidated industrial water treatment scale; a newer but rapidly scaling entrant in data-center liquid cooling via CoolIT

moat_factors.description: Proprietary dispensing equipment, digital sensors, and integrated chemical programs are embedded in customer plants and kitchens; switching requires re-qualification, retraining, and compliance re-validation, discouraging churn
~48,000+ associates including a dedicated field service/sales organization providing on-site technical support that smaller chemical suppliers cannot replicate, creating a relationship-based moat

Large R&D and regulatory registration base across water, food safety, and infection-prevention chemistries lets Ecolab serve highly regulated end markets (healthcare, food & beverage) that smaller players struggle to service globally
Deep experience navigating food-safety, water-discharge, and biocide regulations across jurisdictions raises barriers for new entrants
Long history (founded 1923) and trusted brand in hygiene/food-safety-critical settings supports premium pricing

weaknesses: Exposure to input cost volatility (energy, raw materials, packaging) that requires pricing/surcharge actions to protect margins
Lower-margin, more commoditized segments (some Institutional & Specialty lines) face pricing pressure from regional players
CoolIT integration and data-center cooling is a new, unproven growth avenue for a company historically focused on chemistry/services, carrying execution risk
Heavy North America/mature-market concentration limits torque from faster-growing emerging markets relative to some diversified industrials peers

growth_drivers: Global High-Tech / data-center liquid cooling expansion via the CoolIT Systems acquisition (~$550M run-rate sales, expected to add roughly 2 points to Global Water organic growth and ~1 point to total company organic growth)
Secular growth engines: Life Sciences, Pest Elimination, and Ecolab Digital, which management highlights as accelerating faster than the core business
Water scarcity and reuse trends driving demand for water-efficiency and treatment technologies across industrial and municipal customers
Continued organic pricing/surcharge actions (energy surcharge of 10-14% effective April 2026, trade surcharge of 5% on US solutions) to offset input cost inflation while protecting margin
Ongoing margin expansion from productivity programs, procurement savings, and mix shift toward higher-margin Life Sciences/High-Tech/Pest segments
M&A optionality, following a long track record of bolt-on and larger acquisitions (Nalco 2011, Purolite 2023, CoolIT 2026) to add technology and adjacent end markets
Continued double-digit growth in aggregated 'growth engines' (High-Tech, Life Sciences, Pest Elimination, Digital) cited by management as accelerating overall company performance

business.risk: Customer concentration in cyclical end markets
business.description: Foodservice, hospitality, and industrial production volumes are sensitive to macro demand; a downturn in restaurant traffic or industrial output growth pressures organic volume

business.risk: Integration risk from CoolIT and other acquisitions
business.description: $4.75B CoolIT deal (closing ~Q3 2026) is a new technology and end market (AI data-center liquid cooling) for Ecolab; execution, customer concentration among hyperscalers, and rapid technology change in the space create integration and demand-durability risk
Solenis/Diversey (institutional hygiene) and Veolia/Kurita (industrial water) compete directly across Ecolab's core segments and could pressure share or pricing
Large-scale IT/ERP transitions cited as an execution risk in filings; disruption could affect order-to-cash and reporting

financial.description: The ~$4.75B all-cash CoolIT acquisition, funded partly via debt issuance (424B5 filings in 2026), meaningfully increases total debt and interest expense, and increases short-term non-cash amortization/financing costs already flagged in FY2026 guidance
Meaningful non-US dollar revenue base creates translation risk; a strong dollar has historically been a modest headwind to reported growth

Raw materials (surfactants, resins), packaging, and especially energy costs rose sharply in 2026 amid Middle East conflict-driven oil/gas price spikes (oil up ~60%, European gas up ~80% since end of 2025), prompting the 10-14% energy surcharge

regulatory.description: Global tariffs above 10% (and up to 145% on China at points in 2026) on raw materials, packaging, and equipment prompted a 5% US trade surcharge; further escalation could compress margins or require additional pricing actions
Biocide, water discharge, and PFAS-related regulatory scrutiny across US/EU jurisdictions could raise compliance costs or restrict certain chemistries
Deal is subject to customary regulatory approvals before the expected Q3 2026 close; delay or conditions could affect deal economics

macro.description: 2026 Middle East conflict drove sharp oil and natural gas price spikes, directly raising Ecolab's cost base and requiring surcharge actions; further escalation is a swing factor for margins
A broader slowdown in industrial production, travel/hospitality, or food & beverage volumes would reduce organic volume growth even though pricing/surcharges are largely resilient
Increased debt load post-CoolIT raises sensitivity to interest rates on refinancing and new issuance

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Water treatment, hygiene, and infection-prevention chemicals are a large, structurally growing global market driven by water scarcity, food-safety regulation, and rising hygiene standards; data-center liquid cooling (via CoolIT) is an emerging high-growth adjacency tied to the AI infrastructure buildout
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate - defensive relative to broad industrials because much of demand (food safety, hygiene, water compliance) is non-discretionary and contractually recurring, but industrial production and hospitality/travel volumes add a cyclical component
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low-to-moderate direct sensitivity, rising modestly after CoolIT-related debt issuance in 2026

recent_developments.event: Q2 2026 adjusted EPS of $2.09, up ~11% YoY; reported sales +10%, organic sales growth accelerated to 5%; organic gross margin held at 44.4% despite higher commodity costs
Company raised full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $8.05-$8.25 (from $8.03-$8.23), implying 7-10% growth, and guided H2 2026 organic sales growth of 6-7% with adjusted operating margin around 19%

Announced definitive agreement to acquire CoolIT Systems (liquid cooling for AI data centers) for ~$4.75B in cash from KKR-managed funds; expected to close Q3 2026 and add ~$550M of run-rate sales, accelerating Global Water and total-company organic growth

Announced a global 10-14% energy surcharge effective April 1, 2026, across all businesses and countries in response to Middle East conflict-driven spikes in oil (~60%) and natural gas (~80% in Europe) prices

Announced a 5% US trade surcharge effective May 1, 2026, to offset tariff-driven raw material, packaging, and equipment cost increases amid global tariffs above 10% (up to 145% on China at points in the year)

Split the COO role into two positions - Darrell Brown as Co-COO, Global Markets, and Greg Cook as Co-COO, Global Businesses - effective April 1, 2026; CEO Christophe Beck also added the President title
Increased quarterly dividend ~12%, marking the 34th consecutive annual dividend increase, bringing the indicated annual dividend to $2.92/share

Modified segment reporting, renaming Global Industrial to Global Water (combining Light & Heavy, Food & Beverage, and Paper) and further split Light & Heavy into Heavy Water, Light Water, and High-Tech operating segments effective January 1, 2026

items.notes: Up from prior $8.03-$8.23; implies 7-10% YoY growth; incorporates short-term non-cash amortization and financing costs tied to the CoolIT acquisition
Follows 5% organic growth in H1 2026; management cited accelerating growth engines (High-Tech, Life Sciences, Pest Elimination, Digital) plus surcharge realization
Assumes full realization of surcharge benefits (energy 10-14%, US trade 5%) offsetting commodity/tariff inflation

items.target: +2pp to Global Water, +1pp to total company
items.notes: Based on ~$550M expected trailing-12-month CoolIT sales at acquisition

guidance.management_commentary: Management framed 2026 as an acceleration year, citing double-digit growth in the aggregated 'growth engines' (High-Tech, Life Sciences, Pest Elimination, Digital) and improving core performance in Food & Beverage, Institutional, and Light Water. CEO Christophe Beck emphasized that pricing/surcharge actions are successfully offsetting elevated energy and tariff-driven input cost inflation while preserving gross margin (44.4% in Q2 2026), and positioned the CoolIT acquisition as a strategic extension of Ecolab's water and cooling expertise into the AI data-center buildout.

bull_case: Highly recurring, service-embedded revenue model with strong customer switching costs supports resilient, above-GDP organic growth even in a mixed macro backdrop

CoolIT acquisition opens a large, fast-growing new addressable market (AI data-center liquid cooling) that leverages Ecolab's existing water/thermal management expertise, adding a new multi-year growth vector
Demonstrated pricing power - successive energy and trade surcharges in 2026 have protected gross margin (44.4%) despite sharp commodity and tariff cost inflation
34 consecutive years of dividend increases and a long capital-return track record signal balance-sheet discipline and management confidence in durable cash generation
Accelerating 'growth engines' (High-Tech, Life Sciences, Pest Elimination, Digital) are growing faster than the core, improving the overall growth/margin mix over time
bear_case: CoolIT is an unproven, technology-driven adjacency for a chemicals/services company; integration missteps or a slowdown in AI data-center capex could impair the ~$4.75B investment
Leverage has risen meaningfully to fund the CoolIT deal, increasing interest expense and financial risk just as guidance already flags added non-cash amortization/financing costs
Continued reliance on surcharges to offset energy and tariff inflation signals limited underlying pricing power once one-off surcharges roll off or reverse if energy prices fall
Core Institutional & Specialty and some Global Water lines face real competition from Solenis/Diversey, Veolia, and Kurita, capping share gains and pricing in mature markets

Valuation reflects a premium (average analyst target ~$317-$324 vs. a stock that has already re-rated on the AI/data-center narrative), leaving less room for error if organic growth or margin expansion disappoints
